lead: A comet is a lump of ice and dust a few kilometres wide. When its long path brings it near the Sun, the ice turns to gas and a glowing tail grows. This page plots seven famous comets on their real paths.
try: In the Orbit player, tap Halley and press Play. Then tap 3I/ATLAS, a comet from another star, and drag the time slider.
points: A comet's tail always points away from the Sun, even when the comet is moving away from the Sun.
Comets usually wake up inside about 3 au (three times the Earth–Sun distance). Closer in, the ice turns to gas much faster and the tail grows.
In 1705 Edmond Halley predicted his comet would return in 1758. It did, and it will be back again on 28 July 2061.
